page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 48 vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, though the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and memory bandwidth capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in image processing and strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation, and ray tracing. Uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 190.66 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems, although its Passmark memory score falls into the lower quartile. Cryptographic and physics simulations also perform strongly, alongside high-throughput Redis SET operations reaching 63.01 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 78.62 GB/sec. Large language model (LLM) prompt processing speeds are consistently strong across small, medium, and large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48s_v6 offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The absence of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage, which represents a structural tradeoff. This server is suited for memory-heavy applications, including relational databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation pipelines, web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
